title: Burnham says he would seek to enter any Labour leadership contest
summary_cn: 安迪·伯纳姆表示，如果他在6月18日的梅克菲尔德补选中获胜，他将寻求参加任何潜在的工党领袖竞选。在BBC《提问时间》特别节目中，伯纳姆与其他四名候选人一同亮相，明确表达了他的野心。改革英国候选人罗伯特·凯尼恩则警告不要将梅克菲尔德作为‘跳板’，并呼吁远离职业政客。
paragraphs_en: Andy Burnham said he would seek to enter any potential Labour leadership contest should he win the Makerfield by-election on 18 June.
The Greater Manchester Mayor made clear his ambitions as he appeared alongside four other candidates during a BBC Question Time special in the constituency.
Reform UK candidate Robert Kenyon said there is a need for a "big move away from career politicians" and warned against using Makerfield as a "stepping stone".
Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer has defied calls from some Labour MPs to step down after poor election results last month. No formal challenge has been launched against him.
A No 10 spokesperson said: "The prime minister will not walk away from the mandate he was given just two years ago to build a stronger, fairer Britain."
The by-election was called after then-Labour MP Josh Simons stepped down, a move he said was to allow Burnham to run for Parliament and potentially mount a leadership bid.
The vote in Makerfield is expected to be a race between Burnham and Kenyon, a plumber and local councillor.
Asked about how politicians could restore public trust in them, Burnham criticised "point-scoring before problem-solving" in Westminster before he was pressed about his own ambitions.
The Labour candidate said: "I can't do anything unless I'm lucky enough to get the support of people here.
"But if I get your support, I would seek to represent you at the highest possible level and give this constituency maximum power and influence.
"I think Wes Streeting seems to have launched a leadership contest, so if that is running I would seek to join it, but I'd have to persuade members of the Parliamentary Labour Party to do the same."
Any challenger wanting to trigger a leadership contest must be an MP and have the backing of 81 Labour MPs.
Streeting has confirmed he would enter any potential contest and has encouraged people to back Burnham in Makerfield as he wants a "proper contest with the best candidates on the field".
Kenyon criticised Burnham's record as mayor, saying while Manchester "thrives we're struggling to survive in Wigan" before adding: "We've been left behind."

He said there was a need to "get normal people in politics, people who care about the place, people who live in the place and people who want to stay here and not use it as a stepping stone for other things".

Conservative candidate Michael Winstanley questioned why Burnham was seeking a return to Parliament after previously pledging to serve his current term as mayor, adding he was "disgusted" and "sad that we're having this by-election foisted upon us".
He added: "We will get rid of Keir Starmer whichever politician is elected in this by-election and if you vote for me, it'll speed it up straightaway."
Burnham replied by saying "you cannot control events in politics" as he highlighted Labour's losses to Reform in recent council elections in the area.

Green Party candidate Sarah Wakefield said there was a need for "serious conversations about who is contributing for a better future for our children, to solve the climate crisis, to get our high streets going, to make sure that we have the money back in towns and villages".
Liberal Democrat candidate Jake Austin said the by-election was an "election for a potential future prime minister via the backdoor and that's not the right way to be doing politics".
Elsewhere in the debate, Kenyon said he "won't accept" being labelled sexist after he was asked about his previous online comments – including about women and abortion.
Kenyon said he was "brought up by women", has "nothing but respect for women", adding: "I've made mistakes, I've said things years ago that I wouldn't say now."
A full list of the parties who have put forward candidates for the Makerfield by-election can be found here .

paragraphs_cn: 安迪·伯纳姆表示，如果他能在6月18日赢得梅克菲尔德补选，他将寻求参加任何潜在的工党领袖竞选。
这位大曼彻斯特市长在选区参加BBC《提问时间》特别节目时，与其他四名候选人一同亮相，明确表达了他的野心。
改革英国党候选人罗伯特·凯尼恩表示，需要“大幅远离职业政客”，并警告不要将梅克菲尔德当作“跳板”。
首相基尔·斯塔默爵士无视了一些工党议员要求其下台的呼声，此前上月选举结果不佳。目前尚未有人对他发起正式挑战。
一位唐宁街10号发言人表示：“首相不会放弃两年前获得的建设一个更强大、更公平的英国的授权。”
此次补选是在时任工党议员乔什·西蒙斯辞职后举行的，他表示此举是为了让伯纳姆竞选议会议员，并可能发起领导权争夺。
梅克菲尔德的投票预计将在伯纳姆和凯尼恩之间展开，后者是一名水管工兼地方议员。
在被问及政客如何恢复公众信任时，伯纳姆批评了威斯敏斯特“先得分后解决问题”的做法，随后被追问自己的野心。
这位工党候选人表示：“除非我幸运地得到这里人们的支持，否则我什么都做不了。”
“但如果我得到你们的支持，我会寻求在最高层面代表你们，并赋予这个选区最大的权力和影响力。”
“我认为韦斯·斯特里廷似乎已经发起了一场领导权竞争，所以如果那在进行，我会寻求加入，但我必须说服工党议会议员也这样做。”
任何想要触发领导权竞争的挑战者必须是议会议员，并得到81名工党议会议员的支持。
斯特里廷已确认他会参加任何潜在的竞争，并鼓励人们在梅克菲尔德支持伯纳姆，因为他希望“在场上拥有最佳候选人的正当竞争”。
凯尼恩批评了伯纳姆作为市长的记录，称曼彻斯特“繁荣发展，而我们在威根挣扎求生”，并补充说：“我们被抛在后面了。”
他说，需要“让普通人进入政界，那些关心这个地方的人，那些住在这里的人，那些想留在这里而不是把它当作其他事情的跳板的人”。
保守党候选人迈克尔·温斯坦利质疑伯纳姆为何在先前承诺完成当前市长任期后寻求重返议会，并补充说他感到“厌恶”和“难过，因为我们被迫举行这次补选”。
他补充说：“无论这次补选选出哪位政客，我们都会摆脱基尔·斯塔默，如果你投票给我，那会立刻加速这一进程。”
伯纳姆回应说“你无法控制政治中的事件”，同时强调工党近期在该地区的地方选举中输给了改革英国党。
绿党候选人莎拉·韦克菲尔德表示，需要“进行严肃的对话，讨论谁在为孩子们的更美好未来做贡献，解决气候危机，重振商业街，确保资金回到城镇和村庄”。
自由民主党候选人杰克·奥斯汀表示，这次补选是“通过后门选举潜在的未来首相，这不是正确的政治方式”。
在辩论的其他部分，凯尼恩在被问及他之前的网络评论（包括关于女性和堕胎的言论）时表示，他“不会接受”被贴上性别歧视的标签。
凯尼恩说他“由女性抚养长大”，“对女性只有尊重”，并补充说：“我犯过错误，几年前说过的话我现在不会说了。”
提出梅克菲尔德补选候选人的政党完整名单可在此处找到。
订阅我们的《政治要闻》通讯，了解威斯敏斯特内外的运作。
